summary:
**PlanetX: Exploring the Sky with SPHEREx**

PlanetX is a website that my partner and I developed to make NASA's SPHEREx data easier for anyone to explore. The website has an interactive map divided into 32 sections of the sky. Users can select a section, explore its coordinates, and view available infrared images. We built the frontend using JavaScript and connected it to a Python Flask backend that uses Astropy to read FITS files, check observation coverage, and create images of selected areas of the sky. We also included features for exploring possible objects and saving candidates for further investigation.

Our project addresses the challenge by making space telescope data easier to access and understand without requiring users to work with complicated astronomy files themselves. We think this is important because there is so much information in space data that most people never get the chance to explore. With PlanetX, we want to make astronomy more interactive and help students and anyone interested in space discover more about our universe.
details:
PlanetX is a web application that my partner and I created to make exploring NASA's SPHEREx mission data easier and more interactive. Users can explore a map divided into 32 sections of the sky, select different regions, enter sky coordinates, and view available infrared images. Our goal was to make it possible for people to explore astronomy data without needing to understand how to work with raw astronomy files.

We used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build the website and Python with Flask to create the backend. We also used libraries such as Astropy, NumPy, and Matplotlib to work with astronomical data, process FITS images, and create sky cutouts. We used GitHub for managing our code and Vercel for deploying the website. Some parts of the website use simulated data when real observations are not available, and we made that distinction clear.

One benefit of PlanetX is that it makes astronomy more accessible to students and people who are interested in space but may not have experience with scientific software. We also wanted to make exploring the sky feel more like an interactive experience instead of just looking at a collection of data.

What makes our project creative is how we combined astronomy, programming, and an interactive design into one tool. While developing it, we considered accuracy, ease of use, access to real SPHEREx data, and how to make the website useful for beginners. Our intended impact is to encourage more people to explore space science and discover what can be learned from infrared observations.
